finding: The current film makes World-to-worker membership visible, but not task-to-worker ownership. Worker nodes and their lines are generated from the 15 agent records, while the 60-task aggregate is rendered as only three independent orbit parcels. The source contains no authoritative task assignment relation, so a viewer cannot identify which worker owns any task without inventing a mapping.
candidate_change: Add a privacy-approved, source-authoritative task assignment relation only if the upstream snapshot can provide it. Render each sourced task parcel with a bounded edge or anchor to its assigned worker and expose the assignment status in the receipt. When the relation is absent, retain aggregate parcels but label the state TASK→WORKER UNMEASURED; never infer ownership from array order, worker status, pulse order, or orbit radius.

evidence.output: Worker lines are created from root.get_center() to each agent position; task parcels are separately created at radii [3.7, 4.25, 4.8]. The source comment says the task parcels are aggregate, source-bound markers, and no task-to-worker edge is created.

falsifier: This finding is falsified if a fresh source snapshot contains an authoritative worker assignment for every task and the current render, without inferred position/order semantics, lets an independent QA reviewer identify the owner for at least 95% of a predeclared 20-task sample with zero ambiguous or unassigned markers. It is also falsified if the source authority explicitly defines task_count as aggregate-only and does not claim per-task ownership.
next_measurement: Obtain a fresh privacy-reviewed snapshot and record whether an assignment relation exists, its row count, task coverage, worker-ID matches, and duplicate/ambiguous assignments. Render at the same 854x480 target, predeclare a 20-task sample (or all supplied assignments), and have an independent reviewer map each marker to a worker; report exact, unassigned, and ambiguous counts with frame timestamps. If assignment data is absent, measure that the explicit TASK→WORKER UNMEASURED state is shown and that no inferred edge is rendered.
